clue.text: Short joke about an article of clothing

indicators.note: about means the trimmed joke goes round the next word
short means the word for joke loses its final letter here

parts.note: a joke is a jest
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tells a brief gag concerning a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like it describes the joke's length, but it signals dropping the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim trousers are a common item of casual wear, counted as one garment.

clue.text: A provider of childish amusement, a card giving evidence?

definitions.meaning: a toy whose figure springs out of a lidded case
a knave (the card) standing where witnesses testify in court

explanation.definitionFit: The toy is a spring-loaded clown in a case; whimsically, a playing-card knave in the witness stand.

clue.text: Extra trod warily, having lost page

indicators.note: having lost means the page letter is taken away

parts.note: to trod warily is to have padded along softly

explanation.surface: Someone tiptoed carefully as an extra on set, minus a page of script.
explanation.definitionFit: Something added is supplementary, an extra on top of what was there.

clue.text: Deleted "brawl" printed in bold

indicators.note: printed in means the brawl word is set inside the word for bold

parts.note: stout means bold or brave
a ruck is a rough scrimmage or brawl

explanation.surface: A word was removed after appearing in heavy type.
explanation.definitionFit: Text that is crossed through has been cancelled or deleted.

clue.text: Old man takes violin to play in summerhouse

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, an old man

indicators.note: to play suggests the letters of violin are rearranged as if performed

explanation.surface: Father picks up his fiddle to perform in a garden house.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavilion is an ornamental garden building, a kind of summerhouse.

clue.text: Religious house in earlier years

parts.note: prior means earlier

explanation.surface: A monastery recalled from times gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: A priory is a monastery or convent governed by a prior or prioress.

clue.text: Passionate tough guys kept in check

indicators.note: kept in means the tough guys sit inside the word for check

parts.note: to vet is to check
he-men are macho tough guys

explanation.surface: Fiery hard men held under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement feelings are forceful and intense, so passionate.

clue.text: Free, toilets on Euston, initially

parts.note: loos are toilets

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of Euston is used

explanation.surface: Public conveniences at the London station are available at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Euston is a main London railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means unconfined or at liberty, so free.

clue.text: Start to make a speech about one mother's ruin

indicators.note: about means the speech word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech
I is the Roman numeral one
mother's ruin is an old nickname for gin

explanation.surface: Someone begins a speech about a single parent's drinking downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother's ruin' is a British slang name for gin.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or start something.

clue.text: Phenomenal heroics must enthral one getting the German comic book

indicators.note: must enthral means the rearranged letters hold the following pieces inside
phenomenal suggests something extraordinary, so the letters of heroics are wildly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
I is the Roman numeral one
der is a German word for the
a wit is a comic or humorist

explanation.surface: Amazing exploits captivate a reader of a German comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phenomenal' makes CHROSIE, and 'must enthral' puts the other pieces inside, between its C and H. The book is Laurie Lee's 1959 memoir.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider with Rosie is Laurie Lee's memoir of a Cotswold childhood, a famous English book.

clue.text: Military planners getting stick supporting senior officer

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the stick sits below the officer

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer
a staff is a stick

explanation.surface: Strategists receive a cane backing a high-ranking commander.
explanation.definitionFit: The general staff are the officers who plan and direct military operations.

clue.text: During Christmas period old eccentric shows impropriety

parts.note: in means during
Dec, short for December, is the month of Christmas
rum is an old word for odd or eccentric

explanation.surface: An odd old person behaves badly over the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is a lack of decorum, improper behaviour.

clue.text: Select English, low in calories

parts.note: lite is a marketing spelling for light, low-calorie food

explanation.surface: A choice English food that is low-fat.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the select few, the best of a group.

clue.text: Stand a meal by river close to quay

parts.note: tea is an evening meal
the Po is the river of northern Italy

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of quay

explanation.surface: Someone stops for a meal beside a river near the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: A teapoy is a small three-legged table, a stand for tea things.

clue.text: A waxy substance, resin found on rigs at sea

parts.note: amber is fossilised tree resin

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of rigs are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sticky deposit is discovered on oil platforms offshore.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy secretion of sperm whales used in perfumery.

clue.text: Referring to a head accepting one who learns with little effort

parts.note: on means about or referring to

indicators.note: accepting means the head word takes in the learner

parts.note: pate is a word for the head
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A remark about a scalp admitting a student pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Handed something this way means given it without effort on your part.

clue.text: Very poor writer on African river steamship

parts.note: a pen is a writer, the instrument
the Nile is Africa's great river

explanation.surface: An author travels on a boat on the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: Penniless means without money, utterly poor.

clue.text: Sounds like first-class builder's weight?

indicators.note: sounds like means the next words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: plum means first-class, and Bob the Builder is a children's television character

explanation.surface: What does a top-notch tradesman use to check a wall is vertical?
explanation.walkthrough: A plum job is a first-rate one; Bob the Builder is a British children's TV cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumb bob is the lead weight hung on a line to find a true vertical.

clue.text: PM's back seen first by doctor, to add strength

indicators.note: by means the doctor stands beside the shifted letter
back seen first means the final letter of the prime minister is brought to the front

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the British prime minister after the war
MB is a medical degree, a doctor

explanation.surface: The prime minister's back is examined first by a physician to build him up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back seen first' moves Attlee's last E to the front, giving EATTLE; 'by' puts MB next to that E.
explanation.definitionFit: To embattle is to fortify or strengthen with battlements.

clue.text: A new member returned, a woman

indicators.note: returned means the word for member is read backwards

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member

explanation.surface: A newly elected member came back, and she is a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela is a woman's name, so stands for a woman.

clue.text: Impressionable singer in Sinatra's hat?

definitions.meaning: the heroine of George du Maurier's novel, a singer hypnotised by Svengali
a soft felt hat with a dented crown, as Sinatra famously wore

explanation.definitionFit: The du Maurier heroine is a mesmerised singer, and the hat named after her was Sinatra's signature headwear.

clue.text: Lace made of gold to increase in price without limit

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: without limit means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to rise is to increase in price

explanation.surface: Gold trim whose cost keeps climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is a lace or braid of gold or silver thread.

clue.text: French river certain to cover miles

indicators.note: to cover means the certain word wraps around the miles letter

parts.note: some means certain, as in some people

explanation.surface: A river in France sure to stretch for miles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme is a river in northern France.

clue.text: Spoil artist in lodgings for carnival

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: in means the artist sits inside the lodgings word

parts.note: digs is British slang for rented lodgings
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter wrecks his rented room before the festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras is the Shrove Tuesday carnival, especially in New Orleans.

clue.text: Inflate article during climb

indicators.note: during means the article sits inside the climb word

parts.note: a rise is a climb
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Blow something up partway up a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise prices is to inflate them.

clue.text: Ample librarian, unlikely dancer

indicators.note: unlikely suggests an improbable arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A plump bookish worker seems an improbable ballet performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima ballerina is the leading female dancer of a ballet company.

clue.text: Competently suppresses state of confusion over in synod

indicators.note: suppresses means the competent word holds the next piece down inside it

parts.note: ably means competently

indicators.note: over means the confusion word is turned backwards

parts.note: a mess is a state of confusion

explanation.surface: A skilful chair keeps a muddle quiet at the church council.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is a church council, an assembly of clergy.

clue.text: Novel written by a female making a bundle

parts.note: She is H. Rider Haggard's novel

explanation.surface: A book written by a woman becomes a bundle of pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle, of corn stalks or papers.
